title: SMC — Putting All Together (Complete SMC Guideline)

complete_smc_trader_checklist.llm_summary: A complete SMC trader needs to know 10 core concepts: (1) Understanding of Inducement — retail trader trap for early order execution, (2) How to Mark Valid Inducement — depends on valid pullback, (3) Inducement Shift — smart money traps (especially on news days like NFP/FOMC), (4) Liquidity and Liquidity Sweep — most important thing for driving forex market (stop losses, sell stops, buy stops = open orders that create liquidity), (5) Marking of Swing Points in bullish/bearish trends (HH, HL, LH, LL), (6) Break of Structure — trend continuation indicator, (7) Change of Character — classical and advanced approach for reversal indication, (8) Fake Change of Character and Smart Money Traps, (9) Price Cycle — Order Blocks and Price Imbalance (FVG), (10) Entry Techniques — Swing Based / MSS Strategy Based / Sweep Based. After learning these 10 concepts, the biggest question for new traders is 'WHERE TO START NOW?' — how to apply all concepts on a live chart.
key_rules: 10 concepts needed to be a COMPLETE SMC trader
1. Inducement = retail trader trap for early order execution
2. Valid Inducement = depends on valid pullback location
3. Inducement Shift = smart money traps (especially NFP/FOMC news days)
4. Liquidity & Liquidity Sweep = most important to drive forex market
5. Swing Points = HH, HL, LH, LL marking in bullish/bearish trends
6. Break of Structure = trend continuation signal
7. Change of Character = reversal indication (classical + advanced)
8. Fake CHoCH & Smart Money Traps
9. Price Cycle = Order Blocks + Price Imbalance (FVG)
10. Entry Techniques = Swing Based / MSS / Sweep Based
Biggest question after learning: WHERE TO START applying on live chart?

structure_mapping_techniques.llm_summary: Two techniques for starting structure mapping on any chart. Technique 1 (Expert): Open chart, zoom out, immediately find the LAST Change of Character (CHoCH) point. This is where the major trend shifted. Start bearish/bullish mapping from that point. Key insight: even if the visible chart looks bullish, if the major structure shows CHoCH to bearish, the bullish moves are minor/counter-trend. Technique 2 (Beginner-Friendly): If you cannot immediately identify CHoCH, zoom out to complete historical data. Go far back and find where market was clearly bearish or bullish. Start mapping from there using BOS rules: when candle body closes above inducement → BOS + swing point. Mark Lower Lows, Lower Highs (bearish) or Higher Highs, Higher Lows (bullish). Eventually, when market breaks a Lower High → CHoCH → trend reversal to bullish. Then start bullish mapping. The presenter demonstrates both techniques on EUR/USD 2R chart with complete bearish → bullish transition.
key_rules: Technique 1 (Expert): zoom out, find last Change of Character point, start mapping from there
Technique 2 (Beginner): zoom out to complete historical data, find clear bearish/bullish trend, map from beginning
NEVER build perception from visible chart — zoom out to see major structure
Even if chart looks bullish, major structure may be bearish (minor counter-trend moves)
BOS rule: candle body must close beyond inducement level → BOS confirmed + new swing point
Inducement above in bearish trend, inducement below in bullish trend
When inducement has close above AND below → BOS + swing point (LL/LH or HH/HL)
When market breaks Lower High → Change of Character → trend reversal to bullish
When market breaks Higher Low → Change of Character → trend reversal to bearish
Same rules apply to ANY timeframe: M5, M15, H1, H4, 2R, Daily
Higher timeframes = more validity; lower TFs = same rules but shorter duration

entry_planning_after_idm.llm_summary: After structure mapping and finding inducement, a 7-step process for planning entries: (1) Stick to Your Trade Plan — choose timeframe and pair. (2) Every timeframe has its own Inducement level which provides Internal Range Liquidity (IRL). Each TF has independent inducement — H4 inducement may not match H1's. (3) After marking inducement, use Premium & Discount (PD) zones. (4) To draw PD zones, wait for market to take out the 1st valid inducement to define a Range — range = from the high to the low after inducement close. (5) Mark qualified swing using Level Qualification — in sell market: the swing where market swept previous high's liquidity and dropped. (6) Mark Higher Time Frame (HTF) POI Zones in priority order: i. FVG (Fair Value Gap), ii. IOF Candle (Institutional Order Flow), iii. Order Block, iv. Hidden Order Block / Rejection Blocks. (7) Wait for high-probability Trade Sessions (Kill Zones). Range is defined when market closes above inducement in bearish market (Close Above IDM) → premium zone above 50%, discount below → sell entries in premium zone.
key_rules: 7-step entry planning process after structure mapping
Step 1: Stick to trade plan — choose timeframe + pair
Step 2: Every timeframe has its own inducement = Internal Range Liquidity (IRL)
Step 3: After marking inducement, apply Premium & Discount zones
Step 4: Wait for market to close beyond 1st valid inducement → defines Range
Step 5: Mark qualified swing using Level Qualification
Step 6: Mark HTF POI Zones in priority: FVG (1st) → IOF Candle (2nd) → Order Block (3rd) → Hidden OB/Rejection Blocks (4th)
Step 7: Wait for high-probability Trade Sessions (Kill Zones)
Range definition: Close Above IDM in bearish market → High to Low = range
Premium zone = above 50% of range → sell entries here
Discount zone = below 50% of range → buy entries here
Level Qualification: in sell market, swing where previous high liquidity swept + drop = qualified level

range_definition_and_pd_zones.llm_summary: When market closes above inducement in a bearish trend ('Close Above IDM in Bearish Market'), the trading range is defined from the high point to the low point. Premium/Discount zones are then applied: premium zone is above the 50% level (sell entries here), discount zone is below 50% (buy entries here). In bullish trend: when market closes below inducement, range is defined, and buy entries are in the discount zone. The presenter demonstrates on EUR/USD 2h: after bearish CHoCH, market creates inducement, closes above IDM → range defined → premium zone drawn → level qualification applied → qualified swing in premium zone → entry taken at the qualified POI zone → market drops sharply showing excellent reaction. Key insight: never enter directly in the zone — enter only in the qualified level within the premium/discount zone.
key_rules: Range defined when market closes beyond 1st valid inducement
Bearish: Close Above IDM → range from high to low → premium above 50%, discount below
Bullish: Close Below IDM → range from low to high → discount below 50%, premium above
Sell entries only in premium zone (above 50%)
Buy entries only in discount zone (below 50%)
Level Qualification: in sell market — swing where previous high liquidity swept + drop
Never enter directly at zone — enter at qualified level WITHIN the PD zone
Closing above inducement is MUST for range definition

entry_confirmation_techniques.llm_summary: Three entry confirmation techniques used when market reaches a High Time Frame (HTF) sell/buy zone: (1) Market Structure Shift (MSS) — 80-88% accuracy. In sell zone: market sweeps previous high's liquidity (candle body CLOSES above), then expansion leg drops below the low → MSS confirmed. Wait for inducement to form after MSS, then enter at FVG in the expansion leg. MSS REQUIRES inducement wait. (2) Sweep Based Change of Character (SBC) — market sweeps previous high's liquidity but only with candle WICK (body does NOT close above), then opposite close → SBC confirmed. Because market already swept major liquidity, entry can be taken WITHOUT inducement wait — directly at first FVG after SBC. (3) Swing Based Change of Character — map LTF (M5/M15) structure inside HTF sell zone. When market taps sell zone and breaks the LTF Higher Low → CHoCH → entry at first FVG/OB/Supply zone after CHoCH. Key difference between MSS and SBC: MSS has candle body close beyond the high (stronger), SBC has only wick sweep (still valid). MSS requires inducement; SBC does not.
key_rules: 3 entry confirmation techniques for HTF zone reactions
MSS (Market Structure Shift): candle body CLOSES above previous high → expansion below low → MSS confirmed
MSS accuracy: 80-88%
MSS requires inducement WAIT after the shift — then enter at FVG in expansion leg
SBC (Sweep Based CHoCH): candle WICK sweeps previous high (body does NOT close above) → opposite side close = SBC
SBC does NOT require inducement wait — enter directly at first FVG after SBC
Key MSS vs SBC difference: MSS = body close above high; SBC = only wick above high
Swing Based CHoCH: map LTF structure (M5/M15) inside HTF zone → when HL breaks = CHoCH → entry at first FVG/OB
All 3 techniques: do NOT enter directly in HTF zone — enter at NEW zone formed after reaction
MSS → wait for IDM → enter at FVG in expansion leg
SBC → enter directly at FVG after sweep (already has liquidity swept)
Swing CHoCH → enter at first FVG/OB/Supply zone after CHoCH on LTF

timeframe_recommendations.llm_summary: Practical timeframe recommendations for different asset classes and trading styles. For forex pairs (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, Yen pairs, NZD, AUD): M15 and H1 charts work well for intraday structure mapping. For crypto (BTC, ETH, altcoins): use higher timeframes — H4, 2R (2-hour), or Daily — because crypto candles are very volatile on lower timeframes and structure mapping becomes difficult. For gold and commodities: H1 and M15 work for intraday trade planning. For positional/swing trading: use H4, Daily, or Weekly timeframes. SMC concepts apply with the SAME rules on ANY timeframe — higher timeframes provide more validity. Each timeframe has its own independent inducement level. The presenter recommends choosing your timeframe based on your trading style and sticking to it.
key_rules: SMC concepts apply with SAME rules on ANY timeframe
Forex pairs: M15 and H1 for intraday structure mapping
Crypto: use higher TFs (H4, 2R, Daily) — lower TF candles too volatile for mapping
Gold & Commodities: H1 and M15 for intraday planning
Positional/Swing trading: H4, Daily, Weekly
Higher timeframes = more validity of the trend
Each timeframe has its own independent inducement level
Choose your timeframe and stick to it — consistency is key
